# Surface map library

Eleven PBR families, three maps each, in `surfaces/<family>/`. They are
loaded by `components/three/textures/ScannedMaps.ts`, which is the
authoritative reference for paths and filenames — **not this file**, which
was previously out of date and described a layout the loader never used.

## What these are, exactly

**Authored, not photographed.** Every map here is generated by
`tools/blender/surfaces.py`, which builds a procedural node graph per family
in Blender and bakes it to disk. Nothing in this directory is a scan of a
real material, and no part of the project may describe them as one.

They are, however, a real step up from the runtime canvas bakes they
replaced:

- **Seamless by construction.** Each material is sampled on a 4D torus —
  `(cos 2πu, sin 2πu, cos 2πv)` with `w = sin 2πv` — which is periodic in
  both axes, so the tile has no seam and needed no offset-blending.
- **Normals baked from displacement.** The bump feeding the shader is the
  same height field the normal pass bakes, so the map describes geometry
  that actually exists rather than a 2D approximation of it.
- **Real structure where structure matters.** Voronoi cell geometry for
  terrazzo aggregate and leather grain; bedding planes with pores lying in
  them for travertine; ring lines that wander, with a different phase and
  tone on every board, for oak and teak.

| `terrazzo` | albedo / roughness / normal | 1K | 1.80 m | `tools/blender/surfaces.py` | Project-authored |
| `teak` | albedo / roughness / normal | 1K | 1.20 m | `tools/blender/surfaces.py` | Project-authored |

Total on disk: about 10 MB. All project-authored, so there is no third-party
licence to honour and nothing here restricts commercial use or
redistribution.

`concrete`, `terrazzo` and `teak` are baked but not yet wired: they need
adding to the `SurfaceFamily` union and given a procedural fallback recipe
in `SurfaceMaps.ts` before `SCANNED_FAMILIES` can list them.

## Regenerating

```
python3 -m pip install bpy==5.0.1     # Blender as a module, cp311
python3 tools/blender/surfaces.py             # all families
python3 tools/blender/surfaces.py oak marble  # or just some
```

## If real scans are ever added

Drop them in at the same paths and filenames and nothing else changes — the
loader does not care how the pixels were made. Only clearly CC0 or otherwise
commercially-redistributable sources, and every file recorded in the audit
table above with its true source and licence.
